summary: Ukraine announced a major military leadership reshuffle, appointing Mykhailo Drapatyi as Commander-in-Chief and Major General Igor Skibiuk as Chief of the General Staff. Russian forces conducted widespread drone and missile attacks across Ukraine, targeting critical infrastructure and civilian facilities. The conflict remains active with ongoing air strikes and territorial movements in eastern and southern regions.
key_points: Mykhailo Drapatyi appointed as new Commander-in-Chief of Ukrainian Armed Forces, succeeding Oleksandr Syrskyi (Source: @UkraineNow/82822).
Russian attack on UNICEF warehouse destroyed over 106,000 units of humanitarian aid worth nearly $3.9 million (Source: @UkraineNow/82821).
Air defenses intercepted 242 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions amid ongoing cross-border attacks (Source: @tass_agency/386523).
Oleksandr Syrskyi officially resigned as Commander-in-Chief, citing the need for continued offensive operations (Source: @UkraineNow/82825).
Territorial Conscription Center in Chernihiv struck by Russian drone (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31806).
Wildberries logistics centers in Krasnodar and Stavropol attacked by Ukrainian drones, causing fires and damage (Source: @eRadarrua/102092).
Russian forces advanced near Nikanorovka in eastern Ukraine (Source: @DeepStateUA/23677).
Mobilization corruption in Ukraine includes $10,000 payments for exemption from military service (Source: @UkraineNow/82818).

sections.executive_summary: Ukraine announced a major military leadership reshuffle, appointing Mykhailo Drapatyi as Commander-in-Chief and Major General Igor Skibiuk as Chief of the General Staff. points: Mykhailo Drapatyi named new Commander-in-Chief, with Yevhen Hmara and Pavlo Paliso forming updated General Staff structure (Source: @UkraineNow/82822).
UNICEF warehouse attack destroyed 106,000+ humanitarian aid units including generators, water supplies, and hygiene kits (Source: @UkraineNow/82821).
Oleksandr Syrskyi resigned after liberating 700 square kilometers, emphasizing transition to offensive-capable forces (Source: @UkraineNow/82825).
Territorial Conscription Center in Chernihiv hit by Russian drone, highlighting vulnerabilities in mobilization infrastructure (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31806).
Mobilization corruption includes $10,000 payments for exemption and $20,000 for release from conscription centers (Source: @UkraineNow/82818).
Putin claimed key economic sectors remain stable despite fuel market challenges (Source: @tass_agency/386495).
Russian forces took control of Artel and liberated Blagodatnoye in eastern operations (Source: @tass_agency/386528).
Wildberries logistics centers in Krasnodar and Stavropol attacked by Ukrainian drones, causing fires and structural damage (Source: @eRadarrua/102092).
Air defenses intercepted 242 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions, including Leningrad and Voronezh (Source: @tass_agency/386523).
Russian forces advanced near Nikanorovka, according to DeepStateUA mapping updates (Source: @DeepStateUA/23677).
Shahed drone swarm struck gas processing plant in Yefremovka, Kharkiv region (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31819).
Reactive UAVs detected near Kharkiv region border with Belarus (Source: @kpszsu/69604).
Chernihiv region energy infrastructure damaged, leaving 100,000+ subscribers without power (Source: @eRadarrua/102129).
Reactive UAVs spotted along Chernihiv border with Belarus heading westward (Source: @kpszsu/69604).
Reactive UAVs detected west of Chernihiv targeting Kyiv region (Source: @kpszsu/69614).
Chernihiv air defense operations ongoing amid repeated drone incursions (Source: @eRadarrua/102129).
Reactive UAVs launched from Black Sea toward Odesa and Mykolaiv regions (Source: @kpszsu/69629).
Multiple rocket attacks reported on Odesa and Chernomorsk (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69299).
Reactive UAVs targeting Dnipropetrovsk region from Zaporizhzhia (Source: @eRadarrua/102134).
Black Sea UAV activity increased with attacks on Odesa and Mykolaiv (Source: @kpszsu/69652).
216 Shahed and other UAVs launched from Russian territory, with 204 intercepted (Source: @kpszsu/69602).
Iskander-M missile and 216 UAVs targeted Ukraine from Crimea and occupied territories (Source: @kpszsu/69602).
Air defenses engaged hostile UAVs across northern, southern, central, and eastern Ukraine (Source: @kpszsu/69602).
Reactive UAVs detected over Kyiv and Chernihiv regions amid ongoing air threat (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69290).

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces continue to escalate aerial attacks using Shahed drones and Iskander missiles, targeting critical infrastructure and civilian facilities. Ukrainian air defenses remain active but face sustained pressure from cross-border UAV incursions. Leadership changes in Ukraine may signal strategic shifts toward offensive operations. Territorial advances near Nikanorovka suggest potential escalation in eastern sectors.
sections.regional_response: Ukraine's military restructuring aims to enhance offensive capabilities amid ongoing corruption issues in mobilization. Russian claims of economic stability contrast with targeted attacks on logistics hubs like Wildberries. Cross-border UAV activity indicates persistent threat to both nations' infrastructure. International attention focuses on humanitarian impacts and Western arms production agreements.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian mobilization corruption undermines military readiness, with exemption payments creating inequities. Leadership transitions highlight operational priorities for future offensives. Russian economic resilience claims require monitoring amid infrastructure attacks. Drone warfare intensifies with both sides targeting logistics and energy sectors.
